title: Multiconfigurational Analysis of Local Electronic Structure of $\mathrm{RuO_2}$ Using Relativistic Embedded Clusters
authors: Zhosan I. A., Lomachuk Yu. V., Maltsev D. A., Moiseev I. A., Andreev O. Yu
abstract: We present a multiconfigurational, relativistic embedded-cluster study of the local electronic structure of ruthenium dioxide ($\mathrm{RuO_2}$), a candidate altermagnetic material. Starting from free $\mathrm{Ru}$ ions, we progressively build up the local environment through a $\mathrm{Ru+Q_6}$ electrostatic model, a bare $\mathrm{[RuO_6]^{8-}}$ ligand model, and finally a high-accuracy $\mathrm{RuO_6}$@CTEP embedded cluster that reproduces the crystalline surroundings. All systems are treated at the SA-CASSCF and NEVPT2+SOC levels of theory to capture strong electron correlation and spin-orbit coupling on an equal footing. While the formal local site symmetry of the $\mathrm{Ru}$ sites in $\mathrm{RuO_2}$ is orthorhombic ($D_{2h}$), we find that the calculated $4d$-orbital energy spectrum and its splitting pattern behave much closer to the higher tetragonal ($D_{4h}$) symmetry, preserving a strong quasi-degeneracy among the relevant $4d$ orbitals. Since the local $xy$ quadrupolar order responsible for altermagnetic spin splitting in independent-particle models relies on this symmetry reduction, its suppression by orbital quasi-degeneracy offers a natural explanation for why altermagnetism is not observed in bulk $\mathrm{RuO_2}$ experiments, in contrast to the robust altermagnetic signatures reported in strained thin films.
summary: This work investigates the electronic structure of RuO2, a material predicted to be altermagnetic, using advanced multiconfigurational cluster calculations. The authors find that the local orbital symmetry is higher (tetragonal) than expected (orthorhombic). This symmetry preservation naturally explains why bulk RuO2 does not exhibit the predicted altermagnetism, contrasting with thin film results.
main_problem: To resolve contradictory experimental and theoretical findings regarding the altermagnetic state of ruthenium dioxide (RuO2).
main_result: The local electronic structure suggests that orbital quasi-degeneracy, behaving closer to tetragonal symmetry than the formal orthorhombic symmetry, suppresses the quadrupolar order needed for altermagnetism in bulk RuO2.
method: A multiconfigurational, relativistic embedded-cluster study combining DFT with high-accuracy CASSCF and NEVPT2+SOC calculations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the local electronic structure of RuO2, modeling the environment using an embedded cluster approach (RuO6@CTEP) built upon periodic DFT calculations.
key_observables: Local 4d-orbital energy spectrum and splitting pattern; evidence for altermagnetism (anisotropic spin splitting).
important_parameters: Lattice parameters (a = b = 4.4876 A, c = 3.1065 A); SOC and strong electron correlation effects.
main_assumptions: The use of the CTEP method and the assumption that orbital quasi-degeneracy is the key factor suppressing the expected magnetic order.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the crystal structure of RuO2 (rutiles structure) showing the local coordination environment of Ru and O atoms.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from initial DFT calculations to construct the embedding potential, followed by high-accuracy multiconfigurational calculations (CASSCF/NEVPT2+SOC) on the embedded cluster to analyze the local orbital physics.
why_interesting: The detailed treatment of strong correlation and spin-orbit coupling in a solid-state context is highly relevant to understanding complex magnetic ground states in transition metal oxides.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Crystal structure of RuO2 with Ru atoms in green and O atoms in red. The four corner Ru atoms form a square plane, while the central Ru atom is displaced from this plane. Each Ru atom is surrounded by a compressed octahedron of O atoms (red spheres), featuring two short apical Ru–O bonds (fully shown) and four longer equatorial Ru–O bonds (only two of which are shown for clarity).

FIG. 2. Cluster model of ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) with the structural formula Ru −O6 −Ru′ 14 −Q58. The pseudoatoms representing the nearest cationic environment (NCE, Ru′ 14) and the nearest anionic environment (NAE, Q58) are shown as gray and pink spheres, respectively. The central Ru atom and the surrounding O octahedron that form the main cluster are depicted in green and red, respectively. The octahedron exhibits two distinct Ru–O distances: four equatorial bonds to O atoms in the xy-plane of 1.933 ˚A, and two axial bonds along the z-axis of 1.988 ˚A.

FIG. 3. Convergence plots for the energies of the 5DJ terms of the 4d6 configuration as a function of the basis-set size (NBS). The energy levels appear in descending order: J = 3, 2, 1, 0 (representing an inverted multiplet). The ground-state 5D4 level is taken as the reference baseline and is omitted from the curves. Experimental values are indicated by dashed lines.

FIG. 4. Convergence plots for the energies of the 5DJ terms of the 4d4 configuration as a function of the basis-set size (NBS). The energy levels appear in ascending order: J = 1, 2, 3, 4 (representing an normal multiplet). The ground-state 5D0 level is taken as the reference baseline and is omitted from the curves. The power-law fit of the all-electron basis set energies is shown as a dashed line.

FIG. 5. Orbital energies of the Ru4+ + 6 Q system derived from the atomic Ru 4d orbitals, plotted as a function of the point charge magnitude |q|. The orbital energies are calculated at the SA-CAS(4e,5o) level and are given in arbitrary units.
